abstract: A molecular understanding of microbial communities requires linking taxonomic composition to the genome-resolved functional potential of member taxa. However, this integration remains challenging since representative genomes from cultivated strains are unavailable. Here, we present a new release of the mOTUs database, which extends genome coverage of underexplored environments and enriches its 3.9 million genome collection with functional annotations. Samples are annotated with a new hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates, supporting customizable sample grouping and biogeographic analyses, while links to MicrobeAtlas provide further insight into global taxon distributions. The web interface has new features for interactive exploration of samples, studies, and taxon abundances on a map. The integrated mOTUs command-line tool enables taxonomic profiling of metagenomes, comparison of user genomes with marker gene-based operational species-level taxonomic units (mOTUs) represented in the database, and retrieval of genomes based on identifiers, taxonomic labels, and functional annotations. A new API enables high-throughput programmatic retrieval of user-tailored subsets. Taken together, mOTUs provides a foundation for advancing microbial ecology through systematic integration of taxonomic composition, functional potential, and environmental distribution of taxa within one framework. The database is available at https://motus-db.org.
